protocol: Three consecutive runs of `mise exec -- make bench-redis` on 2026-11-20 on the 0.7.0 source: format 3 commits with one generation flush, head and generation files kept open between commits, blocking reads of up to 16 KiB, one flock per connection for shared locks, defuss-dson 1.5.1 and defuss-storage 0.4.1, whose native adapter flushes with fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) under Bun on macOS as Node.js does. Batches carry 5000 writes, the other workloads 1000 records. Each figure in docs/PERFORMANCE.md is the median of the three per-run medians.

runs.server: Redis server v=8.10.3 sha=00000000:1 malloc=libc bits=64 build=7ed7cf7af45c45bc
runs.protocol: Two warmup rounds, 7 measured rounds, 1000 records of about 130 JSON bytes, and atomic batches of 5000 writes; the engine that runs first alternates per round, and each engine's turn starts after a full garbage collection. Redis runs on loopback TCP with the node-redis client; defuss-dbsonl runs in the measuring process. durable: native asynchronous file backend vs appendfsync always; volatile: memory backend vs no persistence. contended: 4 writers, each with its own Redis connection, retry until 1000 transfers commit.
